sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Replace the formula tolerance sum with an actual absolute fallback, e.g. compare ABS(?factor - ?expected) against IF((0.000001 * ABS(?expected)) > 0.000000000001, (0.000001 * ABS(?expected)), 0.000000000001); adding the tolerances is more permissive and can accidentally pass an invalid f2 value. Also constrain nltl:materialApprovalStatus with sh:class nltl:evidenceState, not merely sh:nodeKind sh:IRI, to encode its supplied canonical range.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Prevent accidental passes from invalid or ambiguous operands. Require designIceLoadHeight to use gen:PositiveMetreQuantityShape (or explicitly report ratios <= 0); currently h=0 causes a SPARQL expression error and no violation, while negative ratios can be evaluated and pass. Add sh:maxCount 1 for qudt:numericValue and qudt:unit in every quantity node shape so a quantity cannot pass by carrying the required unit alongside another unit. Also make each plating-level formula/alternative operand single-valued, especially specialSurfaceCoatingMaintained and materialApprovalStatus, so conflicting true/false or approved/rejected values cannot satisfy the existential exceptions.

Deterministic validation prevents acceptance. Fix: Shape targets generic benchmarkEntity despite the authoritative requirement target owner plating
Semantic validator feedback: Replace sh:targetClass nltl:benchmarkEntity with the canonical plating owner class; that term is absent from the supplied scoped vocabulary and must be located. Remove sh:maxInclusive 2.0 from the corrosion quantity shape and encode the alternative as: addition >= 2 mm passes, while addition < 2 mm requires both maintained coating=true and approved status. Restructure the steel rule so approval permits substitution only for a different steel grade, not invalid values for the named normal- or high-strength grades: normal-strength requires 235 MPa, high-strength requires at least 315 MPa, and another grade requires an approved actual value.

Replace the formula tolerance sum with an actual absolute fallback, e.g. compare ABS(?factor - ?expected) against IF((0.000001 * ABS(?expected)) > 0.000000000001, (0.000001 * ABS(?expected)), 0.000000000001); adding the tolerances is more permissive and can accidentally pass an invalid f2 value. Also constrain nltl:materialApprovalStatus with sh:class nltl:evidenceState, not merely sh:nodeKind sh:IRI, to encode its supplied canonical range.
